entries.261a3fbc4e33510b: This division, at the core of the printing business, handles everything from books, magazines and promotional materials to IC cards and payments, digital marketing, and event and store creation. Its offerings include books, magazines, textbooks and e-books; printed matter such as flyers, catalogues and calendars; BPO services that undertake corporate operations and contact centres; IC card, authentication and security products and services; sublimation-type and melt-type thermal transfer products; ID photo booths; and book sales and library operation. In the fiscal year ended March 2026, revenue from external customers was ¥748,674 million (up 4.9% year on year), making it the largest of the company's three reportable segments. It rose from ¥713,977 million in the previous year. From the current period, a change in segment classification moved some equity-method affiliates from the 'adjustments' category into this division, and the prior-period figures have been restated under the revised classification. Among its principal affiliates, Maruzen CHI Holdings, Intelligent Wave and BIPROGY are listed on the Tokyo Stock Exchange.
entries.2f48026df38bdac7: The company is executing a three-year medium-term management plan starting from the fiscal year beginning April 2026, and its business strategy calls for "expanding focus businesses and promoting structural reform." It designates information security-related, photo imaging-related, mobility-related, industrial high-functionality materials-related, digital interface-related and semiconductor-related businesses as "focus businesses," and states that it will invest actively in them. The company will strengthen profitability of the "foundation businesses" and the "restructuring businesses," and states that in the restructuring businesses it will consider reducing or withdrawing from products and services with limited room for growth. Businesses expected to grow in the future will be developed as "growth potential businesses," and the company positions medical and healthcare-related businesses as one of them. On the financial side, the company plans to create funds for growth investment by reducing assets such as cross-shareholdings and by compressing cash on hand, and to allocate them to capital expenditure and to M&A in focus businesses and their surrounding fields.

entries.5f999eeec3944c5d: This field covers photomasks and other products used in semiconductor manufacturing. In the fiscal year ended March 2026, with market conditions holding firm, the field expanded its business through active investment and exceeded the previous year. It is working to expand into cutting-edge areas such as photomasks for EUV (extreme ultraviolet) lithography and nanoimprinting. In December 2025, it started operating a pilot line for TGV (through-glass via) glass core substrates for next-generation semiconductor packages at the Kuki Plant (Saitama Prefecture), and from January 2026 began providing high-quality samples.

entries.d64e8137f5af84e5: This field covers components for displays. Metal masks for organic EL display manufacturing benefited from large metal masks for eighth-generation-size glass substrates, whose production began at the Kurosaki Plant (Fukuoka Prefecture) in May 2024; however, demand fell in the fourth quarter of the fiscal year ended March 2026 following production cuts for mid- to low-end smartphones caused by a shortage of semiconductor memory. Optical films for displays held firm, as the shipment area widened with the increasing size of liquid crystal TV panels, and a coating system compatible with 2,500mm widths, whose production began at the Mihara Plant (Hiroshima Prefecture) in September 2025, also contributed; the field as a whole exceeded the previous year.

In content-related business, it worked on touring events and merchandise sales using IP popular in Japan and overseas, and on overseas expansion of IP originating in Japan. In XR communication-related business, it has expanded its region-linked XR services, centred on education and government services, and is advancing their provision to local governments and other bodies.
entries.efaf4a14629b2093: This field handles components for batteries and solar cells, decorative films and molded parts for automobiles, and interior and exterior materials for buildings. In the fiscal year ended March 2026, battery pouches for lithium-ion batteries grew mainly through new products for IT uses such as smartphones and tablets, while for in-vehicle use, EV sales fell owing to policy changes in the United States and battery demand was weak. Solar cell encapsulants exceeded the previous year, helped by the introduction in October 2025 of a production line at the Izumizaki Plant (Fukushima Prefecture) that increases production capacity to approximately 2 times the previous level. Decorative films for automobiles were firm, mainly for interiors; the interior and exterior material "Artech" and interior materials for the domestic market were flat compared with the previous year, and interior materials for overseas markets fell below the previous year owing to the effect of worsening market conditions and other factors. In October 2025, the mobility-related and living-space-related businesses were integrated.

entries.fb598fc125c76f5e: This division makes products used in daily life and industry, from battery and solar cell components, food and pharmaceutical packaging, interior and exterior materials for homes and automobiles, and contract manufacturing of pharmaceuticals to beverages. It handles lithium-ion battery pouches, solar cell components, transparent barrier films, various packaging materials, cups, plastic bottles, laminate tubes, aseptic filling systems, interior and exterior materials for homes, stores, vehicles and home appliances, molded automotive parts, contract manufacturing of pharmaceutical intermediates and drugs, and beverages such as carbonated soft drinks and coffee drinks. In the fiscal year ended March 2026, revenue from external customers was ¥512,092 million (up 3.3% year on year), making it the second-largest of the company's three reportable segments. It rose from ¥495,855 million in the previous year. Among its principal affiliates, Hokkaido Coca-Cola Bottling Co., Ltd. is listed on the Tokyo Stock Exchange and the Sapporo Securities Exchange.
